/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 03 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2590 (-58)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3821 (-142)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1866 (-8)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1846 (-10)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1014 (0)

CAPESIZE
The Capesize market lost some ground today, with the BCI 182 5TC falling by $1,293 to $34,651. The Pacific continued to soften, with C5 slipping $0.575 to $13.225, while C3 eased $0.670 to $35.890 amid a quieter South Atlantic. In the Pacific, two miners were active, although the fixing activity seen yesterday has done little to significantly dent the available tonnage list, which has yet to shorten. With bids around $13.00, offers gradually slipped to $13.50 before one miner was reported to have fixed 4–5 vessels at around $13.25. Another miner was also reported to have paid $13.15 for a Newcastlemax. Despite these fixtures, sentiment remained softer, with the volume of fixing failing to translate into a meaningful tightening of prompt tonnage. Conditions from South Brazil and West Africa to China remained subdued, with a lack of fresh bids leaving a sizeable gap between owners and charterers. There was talk of an operator bidding around $35.25, although offers were said to be closer to $36.50–$37.00, keeping meaningful fixing activity at bay. In contrast, the North Atlantic found some support from a couple of fresh tender cargoes, helping sentiment, while the Fronthaul market appeared relatively well supported.

PANAMAX
Atlantic activity remained limited, although brokers highlighted a shorter tonnage list off the North Continent and West Mediterranean compared with last week, lending some support to sentiment and potentially strengthening Owners’ position. Fronthaul volumes also remained low, in line with yesterday, though Owners were said to be resisting the lower bids currently in the market. Consequently, a wider bid-offer spread was reported across both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes. In the Pacific, an increase in demand resulted in slightly firmer sentiment, while greater optimism from EC South America provided tonnage with more employment options. More fixtures emerged for the shorter mineral trades from Indonesia, while increased demand from Australia provided further support to the view that market levels may be finding a floor. The North Pacific remained relatively slower, although sources also noted an improvement in sentiment. The Basic Faith (82,029 2025) open Zhuhai 5 November was reported to have fixed, but no other details surfaced. The P5TC fell by $76 to $16,791.

SUPRAMAX
All routes were negative today as the 11TC average dropped $122 to finish at $23,336. Even the Pacific which had been so resistant recently succumbed to a lack of activity, with NoPac demand said to have tailed off and the backhaul market unable to support lengthening tonnage list. South East Asia came under pressure from vessels in India, as the Indian Ocean seemed bereft of fresh enquiry, with the Obe Odyssey (64,205 2024) Paradip 2 November said to be on subjects for a trip via Indonesia back to West coast India at around $22,000 with BG Shipping. Atlantic rates appear to be slowly eroding across the board rather than any significant drops, although sources say that activity from North America has increased again. The Feng Shun Hai (63,778 2026) was said to be on subjects basis delivery SW Pass mid November dates for a trip China with grains at $27,000 with ADM and ABCML were linked to the Genco Weatherly (61,556 2014) open Newington mid November on subjects delivery Baie Comeau for a trip West Africa with grains at $28,000. The Ogba (63,488 2015) went on subjects delivery New Orleans for a trip Italy with grains at $31,000 with Olam and there was a rumour of a 57,000-dwt being fixed ex US Gulf for trans Atlantic grains at $24,000, but no further details emerged.

HANDYSIZE
The day was described as dull by a source, with the upcoming Eisbeinessen partly to blame, as some participants are already making their way to Hamburg. The HS7TC was slightly up to reach $18,252, with both backhauls improving with talk of $15,000 fixed ex Mediterranean and $19,250 from the Continent into North America, however further details failed to emerge. Opinion on North America appeared divided, with some saying the US Gulf was firming, whilst others disagreed and believed it was softening, resulting in a flat return in the index today. East coast South America softened slightly with rates said to be clearly in the $20,000’s now on the BHSI38 type, after the area being so bullish last week. There was a holiday in Japan today, but the market in Asia was subdued anyway, with little evidence of much changes in present levels during light trading.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles
In the week to 30 October, Chinese iron ore stockpiles edged 0.2 Mt higher to 163.6 Mt, according to 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. Meanwhile, inventories stood 18.4 Mt above the same period last year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a volatile session, with heavy morning weakness followed by a strong afternoon recovery across the front months. Nov opened at 34,500 before falling to 33,500, with substantial volume at the lows, before recovering to 34,500 late. Dec traded down to 34,200 before rallying strongly to 35,250, with heavy afternoon activity around 35,000–35,250. The nov/dec spread opened trading around -750 closing around -1250. Q1 27 weakened from 27,400 to 27,150 before recovering to 27,500, with several large clips clearing. Q2 27 traded between 32,000–32,150. Cal 27 saw significant volume around 30,400–30,500. Cal 28 weakened from 26,750 to 26,500 before recovering to 26,650.

PMX
PMX saw a mixed session, with early strength giving way to afternoon weakness before a late recovery across the curve. Nov opened at 17,400 before reaching 17,900, then fell back to 17,450. Heavy volume traded around 17,500–17,650, including a 300-lot print at 17,650, before recovering to 17,800 late. Dec traded between 18,000–18,350, with most volume around 18,100–18,250, last printing at 18,300. nov/dec traded to start around -500, then -550 closing wider at the end of the day. HOWEVER, AS SPOT TONNAGE CONTINUED TO BUILD, IT QUICKLY BECAME APPARENT THAT THESE LEVELS WOULD BE DIFFICULT TO REPRODUCE. BIDS SLIPPED TO THE $18K BKI CJK RANGE BY MIDWEEK. BY THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK, BIDS WERE INCREASINGLY HARD TO COME BY AND FIXTURES CONCLUDED AROUND USD 18.5K-19K BKI-CJK FOR TONNAGE ON THE MORE PROMPT SIDE. EAUS OPENED THE WEEK ON FIRMER FOOTING COMPARED TO NOPAC, CONTINUING TO COMMAND A PREMIUM OVER LONGER GRAIN ROUNDS. EARLY-WEEK LEVELS STOOD AT $19K BID VS $21K BKI CJK OFFERED FOR

SEASON AND A DWINDLING ATLANTIC MARKET. EAUS/INDIA WAS CLIPPED AROUND $21K BKI CJK MIDWEEK, ALTHOUGH CARGO FLOW REMAINED LIMITED, MAKING THIS A MORE OPPORTUNISTIC BUY. THIS WAS MAINLY OFF THE BACK OF SPOT CARGO FREIGHT IMPROVING ON THE BACK OF FIRMER BUNKERS, CHARTERERS WERE ABLE TO STRETCH SLIGHTLY HIGHER. AUSSIE GRAIN DEMAND ALSO CONTINUED TO PROVIDE A STEADY FLOW OF ENQUIRY, ALTHOUGH THE ABUNDANCE OF GRAIN CLEAN SHIPS MEANT THERE WAS LITTLE PREMIUM OVER STANDARD ROUNDS. INDO REMAINED DIFFICULT TO GAUGE, WITH OPERATORS FINDING THE ARBITRAGE INCREASINGLY CHALLENGING. INDO/SCHINA DEMAND WAS LIMITED AND THERE WAS A SEVERE LACK OF BALLAST INCENTIVE. FUNDAMENTALS OFFERED LITTLE ENCOURAGEMENT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK, WITH OWNERS LOWERING OFFERS INTO THE MID-HIGH TEENS BY WEDNESDAY/THURSDAY. OCCASIONAL PREMIUMS WERE PAID FOR INDO/PHILIPPINES WHEN CHARTERERS WERE TIGHT ON DATES AND UNDER PRESSURE TO COVER. A LARGE PROPORTION OF DEMAND REMAINED REDELIVERY INDIA-BOUND, YET OWNERS SHOWED LIMITED APPETITE TO REPOSITION, LEAVING RELATIVELY FEW EXCHANGE OPPORTUNITIES IN THE MARKET. OVERALL, SENTIMENT REMAINS FIRMLY NEGATIVE HEADING INTO THE COMING WEEK. TONNAGE IS YET TO CLEAR OUT AND WITH LITTLE SUPPORT COMING FROM THE ATLANTIC, THERE IS LIMITED INDICATION OF ANY MEANINGFUL RECOVERY IN THE NEAR TERM. Simpson Spence Young Ltd T: +44 (0)20 7977
